einzeiler: Reflections on Gloria Steinem, evolutionary perspectives on feminism, and animal behavior.
kurzfassung: Bret Weinstein and Heather Heying discuss the legacy of the late Gloria Steinem, examining second-wave feminism, advertising ethics, and historical shifts in gender dynamics. They analyze the evolutionary and behavioral differences between men and women, particularly regarding competition and scientific inquiry. Additionally, they explore the psychological dynamics of human grief and the distinct evolutionary relationships humans share with dogs versus cats.
stichpunkte: Discussion of Gloria Steinem's life, her investigative journalism, and her impact on second-wave feminism
Critique of historical articles in Ms. Magazine regarding gender roles and eco-feminism
Analysis of sex differences in competition, contrasting overt male styles with covert female styles
Evaluation of the scientific method, meritocracy, and the influence of postmodernism on academic disciplines
Examination of the evolutionary bonds between humans and domesticated animals, specifically dogs and cats
Personal reflections on processing grief following the loss of their dog Maddie

beschreibung:
On this, our 342nd Evolutionary Lens livestream, we discuss men, women, and feminism; and the love of our pets. Gloria Steinem died at 92 this week. She exposed working conditions at Playboy clubs in the 1960s by going undercover as a bunny; founded Ms. Magazine in the 1970s; took Ms. ad free in the 1990s, and became a feminist icon. We discuss her legacy, both good and bad. Then: cats, dogs, and the differences between them.
